answer: The pigment multiplier is published, charged in echo, and ripple lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 10 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 2511 identities would post 3104 proofs and burn roughly 31 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
